limitations_and_items_before_training: This is a synthetic source and autograd review. No learned segmentation, identity accuracy, game competence, calibration, transfer, throughput or gate result is established.

G uses local motion agreement. Transitive chains can join distant motion values; own foreground and flow errors can merge or split physical objects. Appearance separation also pushes similar but disconnected objects apart.

Exact collapsed representations are stationary for the disclosed G margin and for the tested I contrastive configuration. A positive loss or nonzero eligible-anchor count is not a guarantee of a useful gradient or collapse avoidance.

Near-zero instance means can create large finite float32 gradients (625000 in the preserved witness). Finite arithmetic is not a stability guarantee; optimization, clipping/normalization choices and their evaluation remain prospective.

I is trained from the tracker that itself uses appearance embeddings. ID switches, fragmentation, false negatives and reappearance mistakes can reinforce errors; no independent identity oracle corrects them.

Stream, reset epoch, exact lag and geometry checks do not attest the actual timestamp/content of images, native paid-frame history, instance visibility provenance or recomputation through current network weights. The collector/assembly must prove these bindings and prevent cached detached embeddings from substituting for a training graph.

Supplied tensors may be detached for loss evaluation. Supervised_anchors counts admissible targets only; it is neither an optimizer-step count nor proof that either endpoint connects to model parameters.

One-sided contrastive supervision is permitted when only the opposite endpoint provides a negative. Coasts are ignored even if they carry plausible predicted locations, and no new ID is forced into a correspondence.

The graph horizon/tolerance, group capacity, margin, temperature, loss weights, observation clock and training schedule remain draft choices to freeze prospectively. Graph and contrastive matrix costs and backward memory have not been benchmarked.
Input float64 is accepted but features are computed in float32. Float16, bfloat16 and AMP are not supported by this reviewed contract.
The new perception stream assembly, memory integration, collector and any full P/C/G/I optimizer are excluded from this receipt and require separate review.
